\section{Results}

\subsection{More reads phased correctly, fewer misphased}

Over the eight chromosomes, 2{,}623,162 reads on the arms span a heterozygous truth variant. pgphase phased 99.08\% of them correctly, 0.67\% discordantly, and left 0.25\% unphased (Table~\ref{tab:reads}). The best of the other tools, HiPhase, phased 94.41\% correctly; pgphase phased 122{,}476 more reads correctly, and left 6.1 times fewer reads discordant or unphased than the tool with the fewest such reads, HiPhase. On each chromosome, it left 3.5 to 9.2 times fewer reads misphased or unphased than the best other tool on that chromosome (Fig.~\ref{fig:accuracy}b). It phased the most reads correctly on every chromosome and left the fewest discordant reads on six of the eight; on chr20 and chr21, LongPhase left fewer, while leaving many more reads unphased (Fig.~\ref{fig:accuracy}). Among reads whose parental assignment is confident, pgphase phased 4{,}369 discordantly, against 17{,}918 for longcallD, the fewest among the others.

\input{figures/accuracy}

The margin was similar on the chromosomes not used for tuning: on chr6, chr16 and chr21, pgphase phased 2.1 to 6.8 percentage points more phaseable reads correctly than the best other tool on each, against 3.8 to 5.9 points on the development chromosomes. In the MHC, whose HLA genes are among the most polymorphic of the genome, it phased 99.31\% correctly, against 96.95\% for HiPhase.

\subsection{Switch errors}

pgphase made 58 switch errors on the arms of the eight chromosomes, fewer than any other tool on each chromosome; LongPhase made the next fewest, 105, and HiPhase 178 (Table~\ref{tab:switches}). A record-level count includes switches that are not phasing errors, so we checked each one against the haplotype sequences (Section 2.8). A switch is \emph{real} when the tool's haplotypes around it pair with the truth's one way on one side and the other way on the other: the phase really changes there. It is a difference of \emph{representation} when the haplotypes pair the same way on both sides, so the tool wrote the same haplotypes as the truth with different records, and \emph{undecided} when the sequences cannot tell, because the tool's haplotypes differ from both of the truth's by similar amounts. 10 of pgphase's arm switches were real (7 of them on chr19), 13 were differences of representation and 35 undecided, against 41 to 220 real switches for the other tools. pgphase's undecided switches lie mostly in tandem repeats whose expansion in the sample no genome of the graph carries (Section 4). In the centromeric and pericentromeric satellites, pgphase made 42 switch errors, against 177 to 471 for the other tools. On the arms it made 81 flips, against 80 for LongPhase.

\subsection{Phased variants and blocks}

longcallD, which calls its own variants, phased the most truth heterozygous variants, 726{,}046; pgphase phased 716{,}046, more than any of the phasers given DeepVariant's calls (685{,}315 for WhatsHap; Table~\ref{tab:switches}). Its blocks are shorter than HiPhase's: 4{,}431 phase sets against 2{,}216, and a median block N50 of 587~kb against 832~kb. Many of the additional phase sets lie in centromeric satellites, which pgphase phases and HiPhase largely leaves unphased (Table~\ref{tab:cen}), and in collapsed duplications and stretches read only at low mapping quality, where the join rules leave each site in its own block.

\subsection{Centromeres}

In centromeric and pericentromeric satellites, where reads map ambiguously and copies differ by few bases, pgphase phased 93{,}251 reads correctly, with 5.4 correct reads per discordant one (Table~\ref{tab:cen}). LongPhase phased 86{,}567 correctly with 2.6 correct reads per discordant one. longcallD had the highest ratio, 18.0, but phased only 42{,}138 reads correctly and left 104{,}573 unphased.

\subsection{Running time and memory}

On the five chromosomes where every multi-threaded tool ran with six threads, pgphase took 7.1 minutes in total, against 18.4 for HiPhase and 3.3 for LongPhase; on chr6, 147~s against 459~s and 92~s (Table~\ref{tab:resources}; per chromosome in Supplementary Table S3). pgphase's time includes finding the sample's own variants and writing the haplotagged reads. HiPhase, LongPhase and WhatsHap first need DeepVariant's calls, which took 122 minutes on the same chromosomes and threads: with them, HiPhase took 141 minutes and LongPhase 125, 18 times or more pgphase's time. No time includes read alignment, which every tool needs. pgphase needed up to 8.5~GB of memory, more than the phasers given DeepVariant's calls.
